Rafael Sabatini, Scaramouche.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/rafael-sabatini/scaramouche

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Rafael Sabatini, the author, died 1950 (Wikidata Q345104; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Sabatini).

First publication of the text used: 1921 (SE colophon: 'Scaramouche was published in 1921 by Rafael Sabatini.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1921, before 1931. Works published before 1931 are in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name one country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, South Africa and Italy. Each of them has a term of life + 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die, Rafael Sabatini, died in 1950, so the text enters the public domain in each of these countries on 1 January 2021. An unknown exact country, or simultaneous publication in two of them, changes nothing.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

- Rafael Sabatini: death year 1950 from the gathered facts (Wikidata Q345104; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Sabatini).
